task: What actually influences whether ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Microsoft Copilot cite or recommend a B2B services company in 2026? Summarise evidence-based findings on generative engine optimisation (GEO/AEO): role of third-party mentions, structured data, Bing index, Wikipedia/Wikidata, LinkedIn, Reddit, statistics and quotations, freshness, llms.txt. Include dated sources and studies.

result.json_content:
{"result":"The evidence supports a practical, qualified conclusion—not a single proven “GEO formula.” These systems retrieve and select sources differently, and the passages provide few controlled comparisons across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Copilot. Treat the items below as platform-specific evidence or recommendations, not guaranteed ranking factors.

• Third-party mentions: A September 26, 2026 ChatGPT recommendation guide calls the volume of third-party mentions a primary signal. A February 27, 2026 guide likewise recommends earning mentions from sources ChatGPT retrieves. These are practitioner recommendations, not a controlled causal study. For a B2B services firm, this supports building credible, relevant coverage and references beyond its own site, but does not establish that any particular directory or placement will cause a recommendation.

• Structured data: A January 26, 2026 guide recommends schema markup to identify business type, location, services and contact details; a February 27 guide recommends structured, extractable content. This is sensible clarity and machine-readability advice, but the passages provide no measured study showing schema independently increases citations.

• Bing and Copilot: A Copilot guide dated October 14, 2026 says Copilot uses pages Bing has crawled and indexed; another, dated August 20, 2026, describes Bing index access as an entry requirement. Microsoft’s Copilot overview also describes its web grounding as combining Bing search results with its model. So for web-based Copilot visibility, crawling and Bing indexation are directly relevant prerequisites—not a guarantee of being cited. A separate enterprise MediaWiki connector (March 19, 2026) concerns indexing an organization’s internal wiki, not public-company recommendations.

• Wikipedia, Wikidata and community sites: A September 30, 2026 Copilot guide says its source mix includes Wikipedia and Wikidata, community platforms such as Reddit and Quora, and editorial/media sources. This is a guide’s account of source types, not a measurement that creating or editing a Wikipedia/Wikidata record improves rankings. The supplied passages do not establish LinkedIn as a citation or recommendation factor. Reddit appears in the same source-mix claim; a Reddit post dated seven months before the passage set is an individual’s testing anecdote, not robust evidence. Treat both platform claims cautiously.

• Statistics, quotations and freshness: The supplied material contains no study establishing that adding statistics or quotations raises citation probability. Perplexity’s product page says each answer has sources and uses a current web index; that supports the importance of accessible, current web material for its search experience, but does not prove that recently refreshed pages are preferentially cited. Copilot’s dependence on Bing’s indexed pages makes indexability a prerequisite there too. No comparable direct freshness finding is supplied for ChatGPT or Google AI Overviews.

• llms.txt: The strongest quantitative item here is SE Ranking’s October 15, 2026 analysis of nearly 300,000 domains. It reports 10.13% adoption and no correlation between file presence and AI citation frequency; its statistical analysis and XGBoost model found the file did not improve prediction, and removing it improved model accuracy. The authors describe their outcome as domain-level citations across sampled LLM answers and caution that results are dataset- and model-dependent. This is observational/model evidence, not a randomized causal experiment. The report also says Google relies on traditional SEO signals rather than llms.txt for AI Overviews/AI Mode, and that OpenAI has not confirmed citation or ranking effects from the file. Bottom line: the evidence does not support prioritizing llms.txt for more citations; first ensure desired pages are crawlable and indexable.

Bottom line for a B2B services company: prioritize accessible, useful, clearly structured pages; make business and service facts unambiguous; and build credible third-party coverage. Check Bing indexation if Copilot matters. Treat Wikipedia/Wikidata and Reddit as possible sources rather than levers, and do not assume LinkedIn, statistics, quotations, freshness tweaks or llms.txt have a proven independent effect from this evidence. The dated guides are useful hypotheses; the large-domain llms.txt analysis is the clearest study result in the supplied passages."}
